review_purpose: Read-only scope, depth, novelty, primary-source, provenance, transfer-limit, and retrieval review of knowledge collections R839 and R840. No code, build, test, syntax check, GPU/profiler work, process inspection, Git action, cleanup, Orca action, or worker contact was performed.

current_context_supplied_by_parent.status: Native16/QSA build and model mechanics pass; serialized three-arm x3 clean 39K benchmark is running; coarse CPU/QSA profiles and natural 32K numerical screen are planned; no final bottleneck data is available.

scope_depth.judgment: Strong fit and substantive depth; 1,613 whitespace-delimited words and five primary URLs are within the 1,300–1,700-word and seven-source budgets.
scope_depth.evidence: The report gives an explicit bank-index model, compares compact row-major, +1 padding and XOR swizzle using one fixed 32-bank/4-byte FP32 transpose geometry, and analyzes how instruction width, tile shape, lane assignment, access phase, padding and index cost alter the result. It separates source-level arithmetic from measurements and includes both an NVIDIA measured padding win and AMD read/write phase asymmetry.
scope_depth.limits: The report's conflict equations assume the stated bank geometry and scalar request model. They are not a full instruction-level model for vectors or another GPU. It does not claim measured padding loss or occupancy loss from the 25% small-tile storage example.

novelty_and_redundancy.judgment: Clear new increment over R811, R832, R835 and R838's prior coverage.
novelty_and_redundancy.new_increment: R839 centers address-to-bank mapping and local tile transforms. R811 concerns block-2D descriptor/message geometry and ragged edges; R832 concerns subgroup roles, cache lookahead, barriers and slot ownership; R835 concerns temporal stencil reuse, halo growth and capacity crossover. R838 is the review that recommended the R839 bank-layout scope and carries the R835/R836 assessment. R839's explicit exclusion of global transactions, pipeline scheduling and temporal blocking is followed.
novelty_and_redundancy.conclusion: Retain as a reusable bank-mapping knowledge archive, not as a Strata design or performance recommendation.

primary_source_verification.status: Material model, measurement and architecture-boundary claims were checked against the named public primary sources.

verified.claim: The guide specifies 32 shared-memory banks, successive 32-bit words in successive banks, and serialization for distinct conflicting addresses.

For Tesla M2050/K20c, coalesced transpose is reported as 51.3/97.6 GB/s and padded no-bank-conflict transpose as 99.5/144.3 GB/s (ECC enabled). The article attributes the improvement to removing shared-memory bank conflicts in this case.

The MI-family example documents 64-lane waves and 32 four-byte banks, with distinct ds_write_b128/ds_read_b128 lane-group rules. Its [64,32] to [64,4,8] mapping is conflict-free for writes but two-way conflicting for reads; the article describes an XOR transform without another LDS buffer.
The abstract reports software bit-vector hash results of 23% speedup/96% fewer conflicts on Fermi and 33%/99% on Kepler, distinct from the report's illustrative c XOR r layout.
The specification defines local_accessor as work-group-local storage; it does not prescribe bank count, bank width, or a conflict-free layout.

provenance_and_applicability.implementation_source: No code, helper or test was copied or proposed. The report's formulas are independently stated derivations under explicitly assumed geometry. Source provenance is public NVIDIA/AMD vendor documentation and articles, Khronos specification, and an original IEEE paper.
unqualified: No Xe2/BMG bank count, width, address mapping, instruction behavior, support or performance is established.
No local Strata source path, runtime behavior, performance measurement or adoption decision was reviewed or established.

retrieval.retrieve_when: A closed profile or concrete source review identifies a tiled local-memory access whose bank serialization is material, and the candidate mapping has an architecture-specific support question.
retrieval.main_correction_to_retain: Treat bank geometry and conflict equations as architecture- and instruction-specific. The published NVIDIA and AMD behavior gives no BMG/Xe2 support or speed prediction.

scope_depth.judgment: Strong and dense comparison; 1,768 whitespace-delimited words and eight primary URLs meet the 1,200–1,800-word and eight-source limits.
scope_depth.evidence: It compares two implemented linear-solver designs, records the materialized MAGMA buffers and the opaque cuSOLVER workspace boundary, scaling, correction strategy, stopping tests, iteration budgets, and fallback. It includes a source-derived storage calculation and an end-to-end measured counterexample. It explicitly separates source-pinned implementation details from published timing provenance.
scope_depth.limits: The word count is close to the budget ceiling but remains substantive. MAGMA source pin and 2020 paper measurements are not proven to be the same exact implementation revision; the report correctly says so. cuSOLVER private scratch internals remain opaque.

novelty_and_redundancy.judgment: Distinct and useful increment over R820 and R825.
novelty_and_redundancy.new_increment: R820 studies recurrent chunk-state materialization/rematerialization; R825 gives direct-16 adversarial numerical screening recipes. R840 instead analyzes an implemented residual-correction algorithm for a fixed linear system with a backward-error stop condition. This adds algorithmic numerical acceptance, conditioning limits and iteration overhead rather than another storage-dtype or GEMM arithmetic survey.
novelty_and_redundancy.conclusion: Keep as scientific numerical-method knowledge. The linear-system solver loop is not an LLM forward-pass recipe.

primary_source_verification.status: Public API, pinned source, theorem-boundary and measured-counterexample claims were checked against primary sources.

verified.claim: cuSOLVER 13.4 documents IRSXgesv, user-set main/lowest precisions, 50 default total iterations, 1e-4 default inner tolerance, residual stopping expression, default FP64 fallback on nonconvergence, input matrix unchanged on successful mixed refinement, and opaque queried workspace bytes.

Pinned source maps SHT to I16/O32/C32 Tensor-Core GEMM; keeps dA for residual computation while allocating dA_sprec, rounds leading dimensions to 32, aliases dSX to caller dworks and dR to dworkd, sets GMRES tolerances/limits, and dispatches FGMRES for GMSTRS.
Pinned source is the GPU FGMRES implementation named by the solver call.
Pinned implementation note describes the convenience FP64-input/output FP16-Tensor-Core solver and fallback.

The paper gives ramage02 order 16,830 and kappa-infinity 4.52e8; under the two-sided-scaled FP16-TC GM path it reports 83 iterations, 0.96 s and 0.79x speedup versus FP64 dgesv at 0.76 s. Its test system lists Quadro GV100 and RTX 8000.
This cited 2017 preprint reports kappa-2 bounds of 1e4 for classical refinement and 1e8 for GMRES-IR; the report's kappa-2 value is accurate for this preprint.
The final 2018 SIAM article abstract states the analogous bounds in the infinity norm, kappa-infinity <= 1e4 and <= 1e8. The Haidar solver paper's cited summary also uses kappa-infinity.

provenance_and_applicability.implementation_source: MAGMA is pinned to immutable commit 630c968a10c4d67a6e679ba942561520160bfc5d; cuSOLVER is identified by its 13.4 public docs because it is closed source. The MAGMA paper's published measurements are not bound to the pinned source commit. No third-party code was copied or adapted.
provenance_and_applicability.condition_number_and_roundoff_limits: These are sufficient results for the named fixed linear-system algorithms and precision assignments. GMRES may not converge quickly. Keep the condition-number norm and cited paper revision attached to each bound; do not present kappa-2 and kappa-infinity cutoffs as directly interchangeable. Residual/backward-error acceptance alone does not guarantee small forward error for an ill-conditioned matrix.
provenance_and_applicability.bmg_limit: All implementations and measurements are NVIDIA CUDA designs. They establish no Intel Xe2/BMG support, behavior, or performance.
provenance_and_applicability.llm_transfer_limit: Transformer inference composes nonlinear attention, normalization, routing and recurrence. Rounding can change later activations and discrete expert choices; there is no single fixed Ax=b residual or solver contraction criterion. The solver guarantee cannot be transferred by analogy, and this report proposes no Strata precision change.

corrections.issue: The report juxtaposes kappa-2 <= 1e4 from the 2017 preprint with kappa-infinity <= 1e8 from the solver paper.
corrections.correction: The report accurately labels each cited source, but should state that the 2018 final SIAM article presents both bounds in the infinity norm. Keep the cited preprint's kappa-2 bound explicitly tied to that revision and avoid comparing the numerical cutoffs across norms as if they were identical guarantees.

corrections.issue: The table says the cuSOLVER contract specifies no automatic equilibration.
corrections.correction: The cited cuSOLVER public docs do not document automatic equilibration. Phrase this as documentation silence, not as proof the private implementation cannot scale internally.

retrieval.retrieve_when: A concrete scientific linear-system solver decision asks about iterative-refinement buffers, correction cost, stopping tests, or precision conditions. This is not an LLM inference retrieval trigger.
retrieval.main_correction_to_retain: Do not map the solver's backward-error theorem to transformer activation rounding or model quality. Preserve condition-number norm and source revision when quoting bounds.

main_retrieval_now.reason: The supplied Main status has no final component bottleneck/profile, and both items are knowledge collections. R839 becomes retrievable only for a concrete measured local-memory layout question. R840 applies to fixed linear systems and has no current neural-forward-pass design decision.

next_knowledge_collection_scopes.title: Graph capture and replay for repeated GPU command DAGs
next_knowledge_collection_scopes.finite_question: For repeated GPU workloads composed of many short kernels, compare eager queue submission with captured command-graph replay and graph update. How do capture/setup cost, replay count, host launch cost, node granularity, mutable parameters, dependency/lifetime rules, and runtime support set the break-even point? Include at least one measured win and one counterexample from named hardware/software versions. Distinguish reduced host submission time from reduced device execution time.
next_knowledge_collection_scopes.breadth_and_counterevidence: Use primary CUDA and SYCL/vendor documentation plus original GPU or accelerator studies. Compare two or three concrete implementations in one table, and report how API maturity and graph mutability affect portability. Exclude in-kernel producer/consumer pipelines, barrier protocols, generic profiling recipes, and model-specific adoption claims. Do not infer Arc B570/Xe2 graph support or performance from another product.
next_knowledge_collection_scopes.report_budget: 1,300-1,700 substantive words; at most seven primary URLs; exact versions/hardware, measurement boundaries, applicability and evidence limits.
next_knowledge_collection_scopes.prerequisites: Public-source access only; no local profile is needed for a durable knowledge comparison.
next_knowledge_collection_scopes.prerequisite_evidence: AGENTS.md prioritizes minimizing CPU work beyond transfer preparation, launch control and validation. Current profiles are still pending, so this remains a knowledge collection rather than decision support. Reviewed R811/R832/R835/R838 metadata covers 2D messages, in-kernel barriers/prefetch, stencil halos and bank mapping, not command-DAG capture/replay. R763's broad data-movement/residency scope does not supply a specific graph replay cost or update-contract comparison.
next_knowledge_collection_scopes.novelty_guard: Focus on host-side command graph construction, replay and update amortization. Do not turn this into another pipeline, barrier, launch-profiling or generic kernel-fusion survey.
